races.name: Virgin Bet / EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cubbie's Dream
runners_data.note: Finished ninth on her only run at Goodwood over this exact six-furlong trip on similar ground; the hold-up style and a flagged tendency to fade late make her a tough sell here against even lightly-raced rivals, and 50 days off does nothing to sharpen confidence.

runners_data.name: Cut And Sew
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has shown some ability with a third at Goodwood over five furlongs and a fifth over six, giving her the best form profile among the non-leaders; lightly raced with scope but her running style is unknown, and Kieran Shoemark will need to place her handily to exploit any tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Gobby Grace
runners_data.note: Debuts for Richard Hughes, a trainer capable of producing sharp two-year-old fillies first time out, with Hector Crouch a competent pilot for unknown quantities; her going preference and natural racing style are entirely unproven, so she carries significant uncertainty but cannot be dismissed purely on that basis.

runners_data.name: Motown Filly
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose second on soft ground at Nottingham gives her a going-preference caveat on this quick surface, but her Goodwood experience (seventh over six furlongs) at least means the track holds no surprises; 64 days off is a query and George Wood will need to use her natural speed to stay close to Queen Of Christmas.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Christmas
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, she will dictate from the gates without being hassled; her form figures of 5-4 over five furlongs at Goodwood suggest stepping to six is a slight unknown, but a K. R. Burke yard in decent 14-day form (7/41) and a clear positional advantage make her pivotal to how this race unfolds.

runners_data.name: Wig Wam Bam
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on a filly whose sole run produced an eighth at Goodwood over this trip on similar ground; flagged as a hold-up type who fades in the finish, that profile looks misaligned with this small-field, steady-pace scenario, and 42 days between runs adds further reason for caution.

races.paceDynamic: Queen Of Christmas is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other horse in this six-runner field likely to seriously contest for the lead, she will be allowed to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates on Goodwood's straight six. Motown Filly maps prominent and may track in second, but the pair of hold-up types — Cubbie's Dream and Wig Wam Bam — both carry flags for fading late and have unimpressive form at this course, limiting their threat from off the pace. Cut And Sew and Gobby Grace are unknowns stylistically, but with only six runners and one genuine pace-setter, the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. This race shape — a lone leader setting a measured pace on good-to-firm ground over a straight six — strongly favours horses racing prominently, as the front-runner will not be harried and the hold-up horses lack the late acceleration their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Queen Of Christmas dictates an uncontested, metronomic pace and the hold-up horses lack the finishing kick to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Queen Of Christmas slots in front unchallenged, Motown Filly tracks in the slipstream, and the pair draw clear of a field that never generates the acceleration needed to close; on good-to-firm Goodwood ground, this controlled tempo rewards the lead and prominent profile all the way to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Motown Filly races aggressively to press Queen Of Christmas and the two fight out the finish between them.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace duel develops between the two forward-going types, raising the tempo slightly but still leaving the hold-up horses with too little ground to make up; whichever of the two handles the pressure better on this quick surface takes the spoils.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutante Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If Gobby Grace, on debut, possesses natural pace to slot prominently and prove superior in class to her more exposed rivals.
scenarios.body: Without any form to anchor expectations, Gobby Grace — trained by Richard Hughes with Hector Crouch aboard — could slot just behind the leader and produce an untracked finish; debut fillies with natural pace can exploit a soft-tempo affair at Goodwood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a longer, stronger gallop develops, allowing Cubbie's Dream or Wig Wam Bam to close late.
scenarios.body: Both hold-up types have faded in finish warnings and poor course form figures (9th and 8th respectively), making a successful late rattle extremely unlikely without a much hotter pace than this field can produce; this scenario is structurally improbable given the sole front-runner and small field.

watchPoints.text: Queen Of Christmas controls the tempo — if she quickens two furlongs out and the rest are strung out, the race may already be over before the hold-up horses can respond.
Gobby Grace's debut behaviour at the start and in the early stages is the key unknown; if she misses the break or is green, the race passes her by instantly in a six-runner straight sprint.
Motown Filly's soft-ground second on her best run raises a going-suitability question on good-to-firm; watch how willing she is to stride into the ground when asked to press Queen Of Christmas.

With only six runners and two flagged hold-up horses who have already faded in finishes at this course, the pace dynamic is unusually one-dimensional — monitor whether any rider defies their mapped role in the opening furlong.

Cut And Sew is the most course-exposed of the non-leaders with two Goodwood runs; if Shoemark can position her prominently rather than allowing her to slot back, she becomes a more live candidate in the final two furlongs.

races.name: White & Brooks Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shady Bay
runners_data.note: Strong Goodwood course form (five of last five here) with a recent win over 10f in similar conditions, blinkers fitted; sits naturally prominent and is well-placed to exploit a contested pace from Molo Del Palazzo and Brighton Beach — the 135lb mark is manageable for Saffie Osborne.
runners_data.comment: Shady Bay caught the eye with a close second last time out and has placed three times in her last four starts, bringing solid recent consistency to this contest; the main risk is whether she can convert that form into victory, having managed just the one win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners_data.note: Grace Harris filly with a solid record at this course (four runs at Goodwood, one win) but naturally races up with the pace; the busy prominent group means she will struggle to secure her preferred position and may end up racing in a more restrained role than suits her best.
runners_data.comment: Oasis Sunrise has experience of today's trip and going, and her recent record shows a third two starts back to go alongside two wins in her last six, though a fourth last time out leaves her needing to find a little more from stall two carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Molo Del Palazzo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Goodwood experience but modest recent form (5th, 6th in last two); with Brighton Beach alongside he will face a genuine duel for the lead and the question is whether he has the class to sustain that effort over 1m2f on Good to Firm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Molo Del Palazzo does bring placed efforts into the mix — a second two starts back and a third three starts back — yet that sixth last time out after 39 days off gives pause, and carrying 135 lb from stall 12 adds to the ask.

runners_data.name: Blue Noon
runners_data.note: Consistent Richard Hannon filly who has placed six times in seven Goodwood runs at this trip without winning; Pat Dobbs takes over and she is ideally suited to sit prominent and grind — her lack of a win at this level is the concern, not her tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Blue Noon has been knocking at the door, finishing second two starts back and second last time out, with experience over today's trip and going and a rating that has her sharing top spot — yet to score in recent starts and a trainer in worrying form at just 4% over the past fortnight are the risks to factor in.

runners_data.name: Hauteluce
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Ed Walker three-year-old who has won twice already, including last time at Sandown; Kieran Shoemark rides and from a hold-up position she will need the front-runners to set a fierce pace to deliver her best, with only one run on comparable Good-type ground.
runners_data.comment: Hauteluce won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims, though she carries 135 lb from stall one and ranked seventh of thirteen on our ratings suggests she faces a stiff test against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Blue Wonder
runners_data.note: Long 76-day absence and a modest record at Goodwood (11th last time here); David Egan takes over for Hughie Morrison and as a hold-up filly she needs the race to fall apart in front of her — the layoff makes her a risk until her fitness is confirmed in running.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back, Blue Wonder brings solid recent form to a return after 76 days, and she has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 135 lb from stall three, her overall profile — underlined by a rating of 81 — makes her our selection here.

runners_data.name: Alice De Clare
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe filly in cracking form (three wins from four recent runs, including two at Goodwood at this trip); Jonny Peate continues, OR of 75 may now be too low, and from a prominent position she could be the horse best suited to turn a contested pace into a clean winning move.
runners_data.comment: Dual winner in her last three completed starts — the most recent coming just 15 days ago — Alice De Clare has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet that seventh two starts back tempers expectations, and she carries 135 lb from stall 10 as the eighth-ranked of thirteen runners.

runners_data.name: Star Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley runner who has struggled for consistency at Goodwood (multiple placed efforts but unplaced more often); from a hold-up position over a trip that stretches him based on recent form at 8f, he needs an unusually chaotic pace scenario to be involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Star Of Dubai does at least bring experience of today's distance and going, and 32 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; however, a fifth last time out and no better than sixth in the three before that make her a tough sell from stall five carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Brighton Beach
runners_data.note: William Haggas three-year-old who won on debut at Goodwood over 8f and is the freshest of the two front-runners at only three career starts; Tom Marquand rides and Brighton Beach's relative inexperience means the contested lead against Molo Del Palazzo is a genuine test of whether she can handle pressure and still finish.
runners_data.comment: Brighton Beach won last time out but ranks 12th of 13 on our figures, making her hard to fancy in this grade; she has run over today's distance and going before, and the 27-day break suggests she arrives fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Lady Milton
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman filly with good Goodwood form (placed four times here); Rob Hornby rides and from a prominent position she is consistent but yet to win at this course or trip — a genuine each-way profile rather than a scenario-defining force.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed form in recent starts — second two runs back and a winner five starts back — shows Lady Milton is hitting the line well, and she has experience of today's distance and going; the weight burden of 133 lb may be the one factor working against her.

runners_data.name: Kokoluna
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton runner returning from 98 days off, which is the significant concern; Charles Bishop rides and she won over 8f at Goodwood from a prominent position, so the step up to 10f and the fitness question after this break are the key variables to resolve.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures and representing a trainer desperately out of form at just one winner from twenty-nine attempts in the last fortnight, Kokoluna is hard to fancy despite a win in her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and returns from a 98-day absence.

runners_data.name: Mohaab
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick three-year-old on the minimum weight of 123lbs with Nicola Currie; form is patchy (7th, 4th in recent runs) and from a hold-up position over this trip she has done little to suggest she can win a race of this quality on Good to Firm ground.
runners_data.comment: Mohaab has managed just one win in her last five starts, finishing seventh last time out, and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures she faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 18 days since her last outing leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Time After Time
runners_data.note: Heather Main filly with two wins on her record but recent form has faded (6th, 11th, 4th); a genuine hold-up type in her racing style but mapped to midfield due to the density of rearward horses in this field — that redistribution means she may not get the race to unfold at the pace she needs.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Time After Time faces a stiff ask, having finished no better than fourth in her last four starts; the one win from her recent runs feels distant, and nothing in the profile screams a turnaround, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 43-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Molo Del Palazzo and Brighton Beach are the two confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field, and with both likely to push for the lead on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood over 1m2f, an honest and competitive gallop is the near-certain outcome from the outset. Brighton Beach (Haggas, Marquand) has the stronger recent form having won on debut at this track, while Molo Del Palazzo has course experience and a front-running profile that means neither will concede the rail without a fight — expect genuine early pressure that sets an unrelenting tempo. This race shape, with two true pace-setters burning fuel early, classically favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can sit just off the speed, conserve energy through the middle section, and then pick up the pieces as the leaders fade in the final two furlongs. Alice De Clare, Blue Noon, Shady Bay and Lady Milton are all positioned to exploit that sweet spot, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the one the race shape most clearly favours. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate: Oasis Sunrise and Time After Time are genuine front or hold-up types respectively but have been redistributed — Molo Del Palazzo and Brighton Beach are most likely to actually secure the front positions, with Shady Bay and Blue Noon best placed to grab the rail seats behind them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Molo Del Palazzo and Brighton Beach push each other hard from the front, setting an honest gallop that softens the leaders and leaves the race open to a well-positioned prominent racer in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners duel through the middle mile, burning each other's reserves, and a horse like Alice De Clare or Shady Bay — sitting third or fourth with cover — reels them in from two furlongs out with a sustained, class-driven finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner (most likely Brighton Beach) asserts early dominance and Molo Del Palazzo drops away or checks, leaving a single horse to control the fractions at a more manageable tempo.
scenarios.body: A controlled, solo lead at honest but not brutal fractions allows the leader to conserve enough energy to quicken and hold on when challengers arrive late; Goodwood's run-in rewards horses who have travelled well throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely fierce and both leaders capitulate inside the final two furlongs, opening the race up for a horse tracking in midfield.
scenarios.body: Hauteluce or Kokoluna, tracking the contest with energy in the tank, would be positioned to sweep through on the outside as gaps appear; Goodwood's relatively flat 1m2f layout does not exaggerate late closers but a truly hot pace would bring them into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses spectacularly and a genuine late closer can weave through a tiring field inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Hauteluce, Blue Wonder or Star Of Dubai would need the field to concertina and traffic to clear early enough for a sustained run; this scenario is materially discounted because Time After Time — a true hold-up type — has been redistributed and may not occupy a genuinely rearward position, weakening the depth of true closers.

watchPoints.text: Brighton Beach and Molo Del Palazzo — watch the early duel for the lead; if both go hard from the off the gallop will be fierce enough to dramatically reshape the race in favour of prominent-but-patient horses like Alice De Clare.

Kokoluna — 98 days off the track is a substantial absence and if she is not fully wound up she will disappoint despite a profile that otherwise suits this race shape; monitor market moves as a fitness indicator.

Oasis Sunrise — naturally wants to be prominent but the crowded pace map means she may be squeezed back further than ideal at the start; watch her early position in running, as if she cannot get cover she may race too freely trying to recover ground.

Hauteluce — lightly raced and improving, but only one run on Good-to-Firm type ground in her four-race career; if the pace proves modest rather than fierce her hold-up style leaves her reliant on others to set up the race.

Blue Wonder — the 76-day absence combined with a hold-up style means she is entirely dependent on a strong gallop from the front and a clean run through; her best form came on soft ground and Good to Firm may not play to her strengths.

races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Fillies' Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Kissmehoneyhoney
runners_data.note: Won over 10f at Goodwood last time, steps up to 1m4f here for Haggas and Marquand; as the lone front-runner she controls tempo but her style fit for the lead is flagged as slightly out of role and her best Goodwood placing came on softer ground, so confidence in a front-running hold is mild rather than strong.
runners_data.comment: Kissmehoneyhoney shaped well when runner-up last time out and was a winner three starts back, bringing solid recent form into this on a trip she has run over before; the main concern is the 142 lb she carries.

runners_data.name: Ammoony
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two Goodwood wins over 10f and a fine placed record; steps up to 1m4f for the first time but her stamina profile looks encouraging given her placed runs over intermediate trips, and David Egan's course familiarity is a positive.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in good heart, Ammoony appeals as the one to beat here — runner-up last time out and a winner the start before that, she has experience on today's going and arrives fresh enough after 30 days, with her rating of 86 putting her narrowly at the head of the rankings.

runners_data.name: Liveinthelight
runners_data.note: Three wins in her last six including twice at Goodwood over 12f, and this 1m4f trip looks well within range; Shoemark has ridden her recently and the hold-up style suits a race likely to be steadily run, though she will need to be produced with precision on the long straight.
runners_data.comment: Liveinthelight arrives in fine nick, winning twice before finishing third last time out, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; the main risk is whether she can defy a burden of 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Kelly Burn
runners_data.note: Straightforward case — won over this exact course and distance at Goodwood last time out, returns after 63 days but Fanshawe handles horses well fresh; Ashley Lewis takes off valuable weight and the prominent style means she will never be far from the action.
runners_data.comment: Kelly Burn won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour, but 63 days off the track raises a fitness query and her speed rating of 70 leaves her with ground to find on the pick of these.

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Three runs for Beckett show a progressive profile but recent form figures of 4-0-7 are uninspiring and she has yet to run on ground this quick; hold-up style will leave her reliant on others setting a strong pace she can benefit from, which looks unlikely here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Marianita faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and returns after a 32-day break, but those are slim hooks on which to hang a case.

runners_data.name: Mother Dear
runners_data.note: Won over 10f at Goodwood last year and stays further, but a 59-day absence for a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is 0/7 is a concern; hold-up style leaves her dependent on a searching tempo, and three runs in her career is a very small sample from which to project improvement.
runners_data.comment: Mother Dear won two starts back but was well held fifth last time out, and the 59-day absence adds an element of doubt; she has the weight to carry at 127 lb, though our rating of 78 suggests she retains ability if bouncing back to her best.

runners_data.name: Pierpoint
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs takes the ride on a filly whose last four runs show no finish better than fourth; a genuine hold-up type in terms of natural style but the pace map has pushed her to midfield because there are simply too many rear-runners in this field, and her recent Goodwood run (9th over 8f) and soft-ground form give little encouragement on quicker going.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, including a ninth most recently, Pierpoint faces a stiff ask here, and a trainer striking at just 4% over the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence; going experience is in her favour, but she rates a difficult one to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Cracking Beauty
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 12f at Goodwood and Sandown for Roger Teal, showing she handles this kind of track; instinctively a hold-up filly but with so many closers in the field she cannot realistically get to the back, and a 7f debut behind her current entries makes the overall profile slightly unresolved at this trip length.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Cracking Beauty faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and back-to-back thirds show she can hit the frame.

runners_data.name: Glenna
runners_data.note: Goodwood winner over 12f and placed at this course on multiple occasions; prominent style should see her travelling in a good spot, and the step up to 1m4f mirrors the trip of her best run at Stavordale, making her a natural fit for this race shape if the pace is fair.
runners_data.comment: Glenna arrives on the back of a win two starts back and was third last time out, bringing strong recent form into this, and her experience over today's trip and going counts for plenty at 124 lb — though whether she can find more off an official 70 remains the key question.

races.paceDynamic: Kissmehoneyhoney is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the outset over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front. Kelly Burn and Ammoony are the most credible prominent pursuers who will likely slot in close behind, meaning the pace is real but unlikely to be searingly fast — the kind of rhythm that rewards a horse travelling well within herself rather than one needing a collapse at the front. Glenna has winning form at this track and trip and should travel handy enough to capitalise if the pace is honest without being punishing. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured gallop — classically favours prominent racers and well-positioned midfield closers who can produce a sustained, progressive finish on the long Goodwood straight, rather than deep hold-up horses who need a truly pressured tempo to deliver a winning burst; note that Pierpoint and Cracking Beauty are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield on the pace map because there are more rear-runners in this field than the map can honestly accommodate at the back, and neither is likely to get their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kissmehoneyhoney dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the pace neither collapses nor truly burns up.
scenarios.body: Kissmehoneyhoney sets a rhythm she can sustain, with Kelly Burn and Ammoony tracking closely; when the field rounds the final bend and hits the straight, the horses sitting second or third have the positional advantage to attack the leader without having used too much fuel. This shape most rewards prominent runners with proven form at the track and trip, making Kelly Burn's Goodwood winning form over 1m4f and Ammoony's consistent placed efforts directly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Kissmehoneyhoney gets an even softer lead than expected and the prominent runners behind her fail to build enough pressure to reel her in.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to force the gallop, Kissmehoneyhoney bowls along at her own pace and her pursuers spend too long waiting on each other in the straight, leaving her enough of a margin to hold on. Haggas horses fresh off a winning performance and returning to a track where she has placed before make this a genuine possibility, though her recent Goodwood run over a shorter trip slightly tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to stretch the field and a horse held up in mid-division produces a powerful finishing burst through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Liveinthelight has strong Goodwood form and a recent winning sequence, and if Shoemark positions her effectively in the midfield she has the profile to pick up the pieces from a race that has been run at an even tempo; Glenna's trip-winning form at Goodwood also gives her a realistic claim if she can maintain momentum into the straight. This scenario is somewhat less likely because the pace is expected to be controlled rather than genuinely searching.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile, leaving a true hold-up horse with stamina to devour the weakening leaders.
scenarios.body: Pierpoint and Cracking Beauty are the logical beneficiaries in theory, but both have been displaced from their natural rear-of-field positions and neither has shown the consistent Goodwood form to inspire confidence; Marianita and Mother Dear have deep hold-up tendencies but inconsistent recent runs. This scenario is specifically discounted because the horses best placed to execute it are not racing in their natural style in this field configuration.

watchPoints.text: Kelly Burn won over course and distance last time out and returns with the same prominent style that suits this race shape — watch whether Ashley Lewis gets her into a tracking position early, as any traffic trouble from stall placement could cost her a winning chance.

Liveinthelight's recent winning sequence over 12f at Goodwood is a major flag — Shoemark will want her close enough in the straight to capitalise on any leader's fade, and if Kissmehoneyhoney's pace is genuinely comfortable, the hold-up timing of her challenge becomes critical.

Kissmehoneyhoney's early sections over the first half-mile will set the tone for the entire race — if she is allowed to bowl along untouched, the probability of a front-running result rises sharply and prominent horses like Ammoony may need to make an earlier move than ideal.

Glenna has placed three times at Goodwood and won over the trip elsewhere — watch her market move closer to post time, as Tom Ward's 3/14 14-day record suggests the stable is in decent form and she maps well to the dominant race shape.

Cracking Beauty and Pierpoint are both natural hold-up types unable to secure their preferred positions in this field — if either drifts sharply in the market it may reflect punter awareness that this pace shape simply does not suit them today.

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ruby's Profit
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with six runs at Goodwood including three at this trip; Tom Marquand is a strong booking and the horse is 14 days fresh, but the presence of Grandlad means it faces a direct lead duel that may blunt its chance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Ruby's Profit nonetheless shapes as the chief threat here — ranked top of the field on our ratings, she brings strong fitness from a run just 14 days ago and has experience of today's trip and going; the risk is that elusive win remains stubbornly out of reach.

runners_data.name: Grandlad
runners_data.note: Has won at this course and distance (1/5f/GOO) and wears tongue-tie, suggesting connections are serious; Jack Mitchell takes over in the saddle and the horse's recent form includes a win just 17 days ago, though being pushed for the lead by Ruby's Profit is a genuine threat to its chance.|
runners_data.comment: Grandlad won four starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions pose no unknown, and he arrives fresh on 17 days' rest carrying 138 lb from stall 5; the risk is that his last three runs have all returned sixth or seventh.

runners_data.name: Rogue Bullet
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with an excellent Goodwood profile — placed at this course multiple times over 5f — and Harry Davies partners a horse that has the tactical speed to sit just off the pace and pounce; three wins from 15 runs in similar going underpins the profile.|
runners_data.comment: Rogue Bullet shaped well when third two starts back and ran a cracking race to finish second last time out, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead; the concern is whether he can convert that consistency into a win off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Brave Nation
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who won over this course and distance last time (1/5f/GOO) and is 20 days fresh; Kieren Fox rides and the horse has a strong Goodwood record, but on a flat 5f with a contested pace, getting the gaps to open in time is the challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Brave Nation arrives on the back of a win last time out and returns in good heart after 20 days, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; carrying 136 lb from stall four, he makes plenty of appeal.

runners_data.name: Silver Wraith
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes over on this four-year-old who has four places from 11 similar-going runs but no wins; all five recent runs have come at Goodwood over 5 or 6 furlongs, giving strong course familiarity, though a hold-up style on a short flat track limits the upside.|
runners_data.comment: Second two starts back shows she retains ability, but three of her last six have been unplaced and she arrives on the back of a disappointing effort; has run over today's trip and going, and 133 lb is no gimme, though a rating of 77 keeps her in contention from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: Ashley Lewis (3lb claimer) rides this consistent mare who has placed in three of her last four runs at Goodwood over 5f; despite her hold-up tag, her placed record in similar going (2 wins, 7 places from 11) shows she is competitive, though she will need a strong pace to set her alight.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Over Spiced faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick turnaround just eight days since her last outing.

runners_data.name: Kiss And Run
runners_data.note: Prominent-type ridden by the experienced David Egan, but recent Goodwood form has been modest — three top-five finishes in the last five over this course and trip but no wins; drawn in the field for this trip and the contested pace gives her every chance to slot in prominently.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Kiss And Run heads to the tape just 11 days after her latest effort and has experience of today's distance and going, which helps her cause; however, a rated mark of 68 and a run of mid-to-back-field finishes suggest she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Sandscreendeliverd
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs rides this four-year-old who wears a hood; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, it is mapped to midfield only because the field is loaded with closers — it is unlikely to race in that position naturally, and its chance is tempered accordingly given it will be racing against the grain of this pace shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sandscreendeliverd has experience of today's trip and going but was beaten into eighth last time and ranks seventh of nine on our figures, making him difficult to fancy despite a modest weight and draw two.

runners_data.name: Velvet Goldmine
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark partners this three-year-old who is stepping back down from 6-7f to 5f after a 76-day break; the Goodwood form figures of 2-3 over 6f here look solid and Ed Walker's yard is handling three runners in 14 days, suggesting the horse is ready, but the drop to the minimum trip on a flat course is untested.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Velvet Goldmine faces a stiff task here after 76 days off, though she has run over today's distance and going before, and placed efforts of second and third in recent starts suggest she retains some ability.

races.paceDynamic: Ruby's Profit and Grandlad are both confirmed front-runners drawn in a nine-runner 5f sprint at Goodwood on Good to Firm ground, meaning these two will contest the early lead from the outset and set an honest, competitive gallop rather than a dawdle. Rogue Bullet and Kiss And Run will look to slot into prominent positions just off that early pace, adding further pressure to the front end and compressing the race shape. The hold-up contingent — Brave Nation, Silver Wraith, Over Spiced, and Sandscreendeliverd — will be released from the rear, but on a flat 5f at Goodwood with a genuinely contested lead, they will need a strong sectional to land a blow and the margin for error is small. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers who can travel just behind the contested lead and capitalise as the front-runners tire in the final furlong; pure hold-up horses face a stiff ask on a short, flat track with no bend to stretch the field. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Sandscreendeliverd is mapped to midfield but is a genuine hold-up runner unlikely to secure that berth naturally, meaning its redistribution should be discounted.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ruby's Profit and Grandlad burn each other out setting a strong pace and a prominent tracker pounces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other hard over the first half of the race, creating a true pace that sets things up for a horse travelling just off the lead; Rogue Bullet, with a strong recent Goodwood record and proven ability in this going, is ideally placed to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace setters — most likely Ruby's Profit — gains a clear advantage early and controls the fractions.
scenarios.body: Rather than a burn-up, one leader gets a soft lead and uses it to control the race from the front, setting a pace that is sustainable enough to hold on; Ruby's Profit, who has solid Goodwood form and a capable pilot in Tom Marquand, is best placed to exploit this if Grandlad fails to match strides.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners seriously over-cook the pace, opening enough of a gap for genuine closers to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: A fast early pace burns out the whole front rank and the race comes back to the hold-up horses with a furlong to run; Brave Nation is the most credible closer here, having won this course and distance before, while Over Spiced has shown consistent placed efforts at this track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Big Price
scenarios.trigger: If the pace dissolves due to early interference or a slow break, scrambling the whole shape.
scenarios.body: With pace suddenly absent, the race becomes messy and positional luck dictates the outcome; Velvet Goldmine, fresh off a 76-day break but with strong Goodwood form figures and Kieran Shoemark aboard, could benefit from a muddled gallop that suits a horse finding its rhythm late.

watchPoints.text: Ruby's Profit and Grandlad are on a collision course for the early lead — watch the first furlong for which one blinks first, as the loser of that battle may fade sharply turning for home.|
Sandscreendeliverd is mapped to midfield but is a confirmed hold-up type — if it is forced forward out of its natural position early, discount its chance significantly regardless of market support.|
Velvet Goldmine returns from 76 days off and drops from 6-7f to 5f for the first time at Goodwood — watch the market for any late drifting that signals the yard is not fully confident.|

Brave Nation won this course and distance last time but its hold-up profile means it needs the front-runners to genuinely over-race; if the pace is merely honest rather than frenetic, it may not get close enough in time.|

Rogue Bullet's record of 3 wins and 7 places from 11 runs in similar going at Goodwood marks it as the most course-and-conditions-proven prominent runner in the field — any market move should be noted.|

races.name: Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rory Rocket
runners_data.note: Two course wins over this exact 6f at Goodwood in recent form is the headline angle; hold-up style suits a strongly-run race better than the steady gallop Veil Of Clouds is likely to set, making his task harder despite solid sim-going figures of 7/15.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and rated below his official mark, Rory Rocket faces a stiff ask, though he does bring distance and going experience, returns from a fair 30-day break, and his record includes three wins in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Raffles Angel
runners_data.note: Best sim-going record in the field (12/15) and two recent placed efforts at 6f Goodwood; prominent style and Hector Crouch's tactical nous make her well-suited to tracking Veil Of Clouds before striking — Jack Jones's stable is 1/13 in the 14-day window, modest but not cold.
runners_data.comment: Raffles Angel has placed third twice in recent starts yet remains winless in her last five, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, 137 lb from stall seven is a stiff ask for a mare ranked sixth in this field.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; headgear worn (tongue-tie), Simon & Ed Crisford strong in the T14 period (6/20), and a recent win at Stamford over this trip suggests she can handle fast ground — the question is whether she has enough in the tank to hold on once the prominent horses arrive.
runners_data.comment: Veil Of Clouds won last time out and arrives here just 11 days later in cracking shape, her trainer firing at 30% over the past fortnight and her experience over today's trip and going a further plus; the main risk is that 137 lb from stall 10 tests her.

runners_data.name: Perfect Location
runners_data.note: Drops into handicap company having run in novice/conditions races; Rob Hornby takes over and the horse has placed twice at 6f on Tapeta (similar pace), but only 2/10 on sim-going is modest — still, prominent style and the step back to 6f from 7f are positives if the pace suits.
runners_data.comment: Perfect Location won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid profile stepping back to familiar conditions; carrying 135 lb from stall nine after a 46-day break is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Consistent Goodwood performer with four placed efforts at this venue in the last five runs including two seconds on good ground; hold-up style (visor worn) means he needs something to go wrong in front, but at least he knows this track exceptionally well.
runners_data.comment: Northcliff catches the eye on his recent profile, finishing second in each of his last two starts and returning here just 14 days later in good heart; he has run over today's trip and going before, and he breaks from stall two under 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Newsreader
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll yard is busy (3/37 in 14 days); his natural style is a genuine hold-up closer, but with the rear section congested by too many like-minded rivals, he is likely to race closer than ideal, reducing his chance of getting the late cover he needs — 0W from sim-going runs underlines the risk.
runners_data.comment: Newsreader has run over today's trip and going, lines up fresh on 24 days' rest, and our rating of 75 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 68 implies — yet he remains winless in his last five starts, and that consistency concern is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Sound And Vision
runners_data.note: Stepping up from 5f to 6f for the first time — all five recent runs have been over five furlongs at Goodwood and Sandown; hold-up style and the query over the extra furlong make this a speculative angle despite Kieran Shoemark booking and decent placed form at Goodwood.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Sound And Vision faces a stiff task, though she does bring distance and going experience and drew stall one; a winner in her last five starts, she was third two runs back and runner-up last time out, suggesting some consistency.

runners_data.name: Dark Alley
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from nine sim-going runs (0W2P) and is drawn at a disadvantage having raced predominantly over 5f at Goodwood; his instinct is to come from off the pace but the compressed field means he will find himself squeezed into a mid-division berth that is neither natural nor ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dark Alley at least showed renewed life with a runner-up finish last time out — just 15 days ago — and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 129 lb burden from stall five, however, may blunt his chance of going one better.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with seven runs on sim-going (0W4P) and consistent placed efforts at Goodwood; Charles Bishop takes the ride and Eve Johnson Houghton has been quiet lately (1/29 in 14 days) — decent each-way profile if the pace is honest enough to set up a strong-finishing prominent effort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with his form deteriorating recently — four, fifth and sixth in his last three outings — Eightthreeone faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures, and a trainer striking at just three per cent over the past fortnight offers little encouragement, despite his having run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Ararat
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran stepping back to 6f having run mainly at 7f-8f recently; Rachel Cook & John Bridger yard has two winners from nine runners in the 14-day window and Jack Mitchell is a positive booking — but his true closer's style is compromised by a congested rear group, and 0W from sim-going (7/15) tells a cautionary tale.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Ararat does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and a rating of 73 suggests more ability than his official mark of 63 implies; however, a run of 6th last time out and nothing better than third in recent starts makes him hard to anchor at the head of affairs from stall six.

races.paceDynamic: Veil Of Clouds is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead from the other nine, Harry Davies should be able to dictate a measured, uncontested gallop on Good To Firm ground over six furlongs at Goodwood. Raffles Angel and Perfect Location will press from prominent positions just off the pace, while Northcliff, Rory Rocket and Sound And Vision will track from mid-to-rear, though the field contains more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically settle in their natural territory — Newsreader, Dark Alley and Ararat are true closers who are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than ideal simply because there is insufficient room at the rear. With Veil Of Clouds able to control fractions without being pressured, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off a comfortable lead, as the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a true late-flying finish for hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Veil Of Clouds Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Veil Of Clouds secures the lead unchallenged and controls a honest-but-not-fierce pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Davies sets a measured tempo, the field strings out on the fast ground, and prominent horses tracking just off the lead get first run; Raffles Angel and Perfect Location, both proven at 6f on similar Goodwood going, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Veil Of Clouds ties herself up and Raffles Angel or Perfect Location travel strongly enough to sweep past inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds at a controlled pace but Raffles Angel's 12/15 sim-going record and sharp course form give her the edge over the leader; Perfect Location, who drops back to handicap company, can also nail a tiring front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Veil Of Clouds rolls along at a stronger-than-expected clip and the pace collapses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Rory Rocket, who has two recent course wins over exactly this trip, could pick up the pieces if the leaders crack; Northcliff, with consistent placed form at Goodwood, is the most likely beneficiary from just off the pace given his familiarity with the track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Denied Position
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches, genuine hold-up horses cannot get clear runs and the race is won entirely in the first half.
scenarios.body: Newsreader, Dark Alley and Ararat — all redistributed from their natural rear position — will struggle to find daylight when racing closer to the pace than suits them; the race plays into the hands of early movers like Eightthreeone, who is proven at Goodwood and can quicken from mid-division if gaps appear.

watchPoints.text: Veil Of Clouds is the entire race shape — watch whether Harry Davies is allowed to bowl along uncontested or whether Raffles Angel or Perfect Location push her harder than expected, as any material increase in tempo flips the race in favour of hold-up horses.

Northcliff and Rory Rocket are the two most likely beneficiaries if the pace collapses in the final furlong; both have strong recent Goodwood form and are worth monitoring for any signs of traffic trouble in the straight that could cost them a placing.

Newsreader, Dark Alley and Ararat are genuine closers likely to be racing out of their natural position today; if any of them get shuffled back into clear ground late they carry a minor threat, but the structural disadvantage is real and should temper expectations.

Sound And Vision's step up from 5f to 6f is the key unknown — Goodwood's undulating track can be unforgiving for horses attempting the distance for the first time, and the extra furlong could either unlock or expose him depending on how the race is run.

Trainer T14 activity is notably high for Tony Carroll (3/37) and Ed Walker (3/41), both with runners in this field — yard form bears watching as context for Newsreader and Sound And Vision's readiness, even if neither is ideally placed tactically.

races.name: Gay Kindersley Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kimeko Glory
runners_data.note: Recent Goodwood winner (1/8f) who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, but the density of closers in this field means she is likely pushed into a midfield position she would not choose; her style fit is slightly compromised (0.93), though her course form and trainer Charles Hills's 1/18 14-day strike rate suggest she retains ability if the pace is strong enough.
runners_data.comment: Kimeko Glory won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making her an obvious candidate to follow up; the weight of 159 lb from stall nine is the one factor to monitor, but her recent form puts her clear at the head of this field.

runners_data.name: Show Biz Kid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with consistent Goodwood form including a win over 10f on fast going and three placed efforts at the track; LR of 29 days is not a concern, and his sim-going score of 11/15 is the joint-best in the field, making him a natural beneficiary if the front-runners burn each other out.
runners_data.comment: Show Biz Kid has run over today's trip and going, and his third two starts back shows he can get competitive, though fifth last time out and a win four starts back suggest inconsistency; 156 lb is no gimme, but 29 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has placed four times at Goodwood but struggles to win (one career win), with a sim-going score of 10/15; wears a hood and has run repeatedly over this course and distance, though his flat finishing position in recent starts suggests he needs the pace to set up late.
runners_data.comment: Beach Point arrives on the back of a consistent string of fourths, with his one recent placing — third five starts back — highlighting his knack for running well without quite getting his head in front, and our rating of 75 puts him right in the mix; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight years with three wins in his last five starts including two over 10f, wearing a hood and returning after 19 days; his sim-going score is only 7/15 which is a mild flag, but his recent winning form and Tony Carroll's yard in strong shape (3/37 14-day) make him a credible hold-up contender if the pace suits.
runners_data.comment: Pride Of Nepal has tumbled down the order in his last two starts after a four-timer, and our figures rank him ninth of ten here, making him hard to fancy at the weights off 69; the step back to familiar distance and going offers some hope, but he needs to rediscover that winning thread sharpish.

runners_data.name: Gone Rogue
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won twice at Goodwood over 8-10f and is well-suited to Good to Firm going; the two-year-old jockey claim for Mr George Gorman (3lb) is an asset, and his ability to travel just off the pace and quicken makes him the standout prominent type in this field if the front-runners set an honest gallop.
runners_data.comment: Gone Rogue brings a sharp profile to this contest, winning last time out and again three starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the main risk is whether he can defy a burden of 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Sant Alessio
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by Joe Tickle (1/5 14-day, small but noted), returning after 58 days off with a mixed profile at shorter trips; his recent form shows a win at Stanton and a placing, but he has yet to race over this 1m1f distance and his sim-going score of 6/15 is the weakest of the front-runners — pace-setter role is likely, durability in question.
runners_data.comment: Sant Alessio showed a win four starts back and a second five starts back, but he has been largely out of the picture since, finishing unplaced, seventh, and fourth in his last three; now 58 days off the track, fitness is the question as he shoulders 154 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Romantic Spirit
runners_data.note: The second confirmed pace-setter, returning after 62 days off for David Menuisier whose 14-day record is 0/5; all five recent runs on Stanton going mean her sim-going score of 1/15 on turf-good ground is a serious concern, and she has never won or placed, suggesting she is more likely to set pace than win it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and without a finish better than fourth in recent form, Romantic Spirit at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, though 62 days off and 152 lb from stall five make this a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Grey Fox
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with strong Goodwood course form (placed twice in last five including 2/10f), a true hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear but is redistributed into midfield here due to the volume of closers; style fit of 0.92 tempers expectations, though his course familiarity and trainer Emma Lavelle's patient handling are noted.
runners_data.comment: Grey Fox arrives on the back of a third last time out and a second two starts back, but had finished sixth and sixth before that, and his ranking of eighth of ten on our figures makes him a tough sell carrying 151 lb from stall ten, winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Platinum Prince
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type from the Gary & Josh Moore yard (2/21 14-day), wearing blinkers and returning after 51 days; his redistribution into midfield means he is racing out of his most effective role (style fit 0.93), and his sim-going score of 4/15 on comparable ground is among the lower figures in the field.
runners_data.comment: Platinum Prince has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 75 suggests he is better than his official mark of 63 implies, giving him a lively each-way chance from stall 8; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and returns after 51 days off.

runners_data.name: Artavian
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-midfield type who has struggled for form recently (2-7367), but his best efforts have come over 10f on soft-ish ground and trainer Patrick Chamings sends him with a 0/10 14-day record; wears a visor and tongue tie, last ran 20 days ago, and while he may push forward early his overall profile makes him a low-probability winner in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Artavian has little obvious appeal here, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and a run twenty days ago leaves him fit enough.

races.paceDynamic: Sant Alessio and Romantic Spirit are the two confirmed front-runners in a ten-runner field, and with both likely to press from the gates on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood, an honest, competitive gallop is virtually guaranteed from the outset over this 1m1f trip. Gone Rogue will look to sit prominently just off that lead, while Artavian may also push forward, meaning the early sectionals should be genuine rather than dawdling. The race shape that emerges — a true pace set by two leaders, with the field strung out early — classically suits hold-up horses who can conserve energy and pick up ground through the final two furlongs of Goodwood's run-in; the tactical verdict is that genuine closers hold a structural advantage here. However, Kimeko Glory, Grey Fox, and Platinum Prince — all true hold-up types — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field carries more hold-up horses than the rear positions can accommodate, meaning several will be forced to race closer to the pace than is natural for them, which may compromise their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Sant Alessio and Romantic Spirit burn each other out setting a genuinely strong gallop, leaving the hold-up horses to sweep past late.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners push each other along from the flag, creating a fast early pace that sets up the race perfectly for horses coming from off the bridle in the straight; Goodwood's undulating finish rewards those with energy in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Player Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not ruinous, allowing a horse racing just off the leaders to time a challenge perfectly through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Gone Rogue, a proven winner at Goodwood who has won twice over similar distances in good going, is ideally positioned to travel smoothly just behind the leaders and strike as the front-runners tire; this shape suits horses who combine tactical speed with a genuine turn of foot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Sant Alessio — gets a soft lead and the pace is not as strong as anticipated, conserving enough to last home.
scenarios.body: Sant Alessio has won on similar quick ground and his rider Mr Henry Moore would benefit from Romantic Spirit fading early, leaving one leader to dictate without pressure; on Good to Firm Goodwood going, a horse that settles in front and is not overhauled is a realistic outcome if the tempo drops in the middle portion.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so strong that even horses mapped to midfield — particularly the redistributed hold-up types — find themselves better placed than usual and can reel in a weakening front rank.
scenarios.body: Kimeko Glory or Grey Fox, though racing closer than ideal, could benefit if their enforced midfield berth means they strike at the optimal moment in a race where the hold-up position is simply too far back to get involved; this scenario depends on an unusually strong gallop and the redistributed types travelling well in an unnatural role — a discounted but non-trivial outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sant Alessio and Romantic Spirit will both attempt to lead — watch which one surrenders first, as the surviving front-runner may get a brief solo in front that becomes harder to peg back if the closers are too far back.

Gone Rogue is the most naturally positioned runner to exploit the pace being set — watch his early cruising speed in the first three furlongs; if he travels easily just behind the leaders he is the most structurally favoured horse in the race.

Pride Of Nepal's recent winning sequence (three wins in five) on going slower than today's Good to Firm is worth monitoring — if the ground is riding quicker than the listed description, his sim-going flag (7/15) could become a genuine performance concern.

Grey Fox and Kimeko Glory, both redistributed into midfield, are worth watching in the first furlong — if either gets shuffled back to their natural hold-up position the scenario favouring them becomes less likely, whereas if they settle in midfield comfortably their chance improves marginally.

Romantic Spirit has a sim-going score of just 1/15 on equivalent turf-good ground across her last five runs — if she weakens sharply after setting the early pace, the rate at which she falls away will determine how much energy the other front-runner Sant Alessio has consumed matching her.
